topic: break in stiff new leather shoes
core_question: How do I break in a brand-new pair of stiff leather shoes? (secondary: How do I keep cooked pasta from sticking together in a clump?)
answer_summary: Wear the new shoes around the house with thick socks for short stretches, flexing the leather as you walk, and rub in a leather conditioner to soften the material and speed up the break-in.; after the topic shift: Cook pasta in a large pot with plenty of well-salted boiling water, stir in the first minute, and drain and immediately toss with sauce or a little oil so the strands don't sit and stick together.
persona: friendly but persistent; chatty and verbose
